about:
Robert Trusko taught me how to produce music.

When we were in music school together, Trusko made me believe everything was possible. Any dope thing we'd listen to, Trusko would be able to break it down, reverse engineer it, and scheme a way for us to re-create the dopeness in our studio on our budget. He played bass in my first band, Many Voices, and we dreamed everything together.

We also went through hell together.

Tumble is about a friendship gone wrong. It's about all the ways that people hurt each other without even knowing. And it's about walking away. Sometimes you need distance to really understand what happened. Ten years after graduating college, I was finally ready to write this song.

Tumble first appeared on the EP, "i'm not scared now". The all of the instruments were recorded live. Classic. Meanwhile, I'd been listening to artists like Noname, Saba, and Smino who blend live instruments with samples. I knew I wanted to incorporate more of that style into my sound, but I didn't know how. That's where Trusko came in. 

Trusko's production brought Elliot.wavs into the future. He chopped and stretched the time, re-recorded the bass and brought in Cameron McCloud to feature.

Suddenly, "Tumble" was a whole different song

Just like old times, Trusko's mix expanded my vision of what was possible in my music. Listening to his mix, I realized "This is what Elliot.wavs sounds like".
